anomalies.obs: The two isolated CAN transceivers, U11 (driven by CAN0 controller U8) and U10 (driven by CAN1 controller U9), both have their CANH/CANL outputs connected to the same global nets labelled "CAN_P" and "CAN_N". The two buses are therefore shorted together on a single pair of nets.
anomalies.exp: The specification requires two separate isolated buses: "two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)" and TVS arrays "on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N". U11 should drive CAN0_P/CAN0_N and U10 should drive CAN1_P/CAN1_N, kept apart.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet: U11 pin7 (CANH)/pin6 (CANL) -> global labels "CAN_P"/"CAN_N"; U10 pin7/pin6 -> the same global labels "CAN_P"/"CAN_N"
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)

anomalies.impact: CAN0 and CAN1 are merged into one physical bus; the two isolated domains are no longer isolated and will fight each other, corrupting motor-communication traffic.

anomalies.obs: The M12 connectors J2 ("CAN Interface A") and J13 ("CAN Interface B") carry the indexed nets CAN0_P/CAN0_N and CAN1_P/CAN1_N, but no transceiver drives those names (the transceivers are on the un-indexed CAN_P/CAN_N nets). The connector CAN pairs are therefore floating.
anomalies.exp: Per the spec the transceiver outputs must reach the M12 connectors under matching net names (CAN0_P/CAN1_P etc.), as in the reference design.

evidence.quote: Connector sheet: J2 pin5="CAN0_P", pin8="CAN0_N", pin2="CAN1_P", pin3="CAN1_N"; J13 pin5="CAN0_P", pin8="CAN0_N", pin2="CAN1_P", pin3="CAN1_N" (no transceiver label matches these)
broken out on M12 circular connectors J2 ("CAN Interface A") and J13 ("CAN Interface B")

anomalies.impact: Neither CAN bus reaches the Odrive motor connectors; motor control communication is lost.

parsed.summary: The CAN physical-layer global labels are inconsistent with the reference design: both transceivers U10 and U11 are tied to the same un-indexed nets CAN_P/CAN_N (merging the two isolated buses), while the M12 connectors J2/J13 use the indexed nets CAN0_P/CAN1_P/CAN0_N/CAN1_N that nothing drives. This bridges CAN0 and CAN1 together and leaves the motor connectors unconnected, breaking the board's primary motor-communication function.
